thought.text: Actuator port 8081 is open. Let me verify actuator health via the container IP and check the public API paths:

reasoning_content: Actuator port 8081 is open, but there's no wget inside the container. Let me test the actuator with a different approach — either curl via the container's network, or use docker's port mapping. Actually, the easiest thing is to test actuator's /health from the host via the container's IP.

action.command:
IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' urbo-workspace-spring-app-1); echo "spring-app IP: $IP"
echo "=== actuator /health via container IP (from host, same network? use docker network) ==="
docker exec urbo-workspace-spring-app-1 sh -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8081; printf "GET /health HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Connection: close

" >&3; cat <&3' 2>/dev/null | head -20

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' urbo-workspace-spring-app-1); echo \"spring-app IP: $IP\"\necho \"=== actuator /health via container IP (from host, same network? use docker network) ===\"\ndocker exec urbo-workspace-spring-app-1 sh -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8081; printf \"GET /health HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n\" >&3; cat <&3' 2>/dev/null | head -20", "summary": "Test actuator health endpoint directly"}
